\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{امانت} (amānat)}{امانت (amānat)}]{\ur{امانت} (amānat) — something left in one's keeping}

\label{lesson:UR-C531-amanat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for turned down, then the Urdu for to turn back.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{امانت}}
\textbf{\ur{امانت}} — \emph{amānat} — \textquotedblleft{}something left in one's keeping\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{امانت} \ur{لوٹائی} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{خوش} \ur{ہوں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar us ne amānat lauṭāī to maiṅ khush hūṅ gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If he gives back what I left with him, I will be glad.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{امانت}} (\emph{amānat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{amāna}, \textquotedblleft{}trustworthiness; a thing entrusted\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{amānat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{amānat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar us ne amānat lauṭāī to maiṅ khush hūṅ gā.} — If he gives back what I left with him, I will be glad.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for turned down, then the Urdu for to turn back, then say \emph{amānat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{امانت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Something left in one's keeping\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{قول} (qaul)}{قول (qaul)}]{\ur{قول} (qaul) — one's given word}

\label{lesson:UR-C531-qaul}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to turn back, then the Urdu for something left in one's keeping.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{قول}}
\textbf{\ur{قول}} — \emph{qaul} — \textquotedblleft{}one's given word\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{وہ} \ur{قول} \ur{کا} \ur{پکا} \ur{ہوتا} \ur{تو} \ur{آج} \ur{آتا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar voh qaul kā pakkā hotā to āj ātā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If he kept his word, he would have come today.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{قول}} (\emph{qaul}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{qawl}, \textquotedblleft{}a saying, a word\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qaul}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qaul}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar voh qaul kā pakkā hotā to āj ātā.} — If he kept his word, he would have come today.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to turn back, then the Urdu for something left in one's keeping, then say \emph{qaul} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پاسداری} (pāsdārī)}{پاسداری (pāsdārī)}]{\ur{پاسداری} (pāsdārī) — keeping to (a rule or a promise); honouring}

\label{lesson:UR-C531-pasdari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for something left in one's keeping, then the Urdu for one's given word.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پاسداری}}
\textbf{\ur{پاسداری}} — \emph{pāsdārī} — \textquotedblleft{}keeping to (a rule or a promise); honouring\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{سب} \ur{قانون} \ur{کی} \ur{پاسداری} \ur{کرتے} \ur{تو} \ur{حادثے} \ur{کم} \ur{ہوتے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar sab qānūn kī pāsdārī karte to hādse kam hote.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If everyone kept to the law, there would be fewer accidents.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پاسداری}} (\emph{pāsdārī}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{pāsdārī}, \textquotedblleft{}guarding, keeping\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{pās}, \textquotedblleft{}watch, regard\textquotedblright{}, \emph{-dār}, \textquotedblleft{}holding\textquotedblright{}, and the noun ending \emph{-ī}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pāsdārī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar sab qānūn kī pāsdārī karte to hādse kam hote.} — If everyone kept to the law, there would be fewer accidents.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for something left in one's keeping, then the Urdu for one's given word, then say \emph{pāsdārī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ساکھ} (sākh)}{ساکھ (sākh)}]{\ur{ساکھ} (sākh) — a good name (for honesty); credit}

\label{lesson:UR-C531-sakh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for one's given word, then the Urdu for honouring a rule.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ساکھ}}
\textbf{\ur{ساکھ}} — \emph{sākh} — \textquotedblleft{}a good name (for honesty); credit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{دکاندار} \ur{جھوٹ} \ur{بولتا} \ur{تو} \ur{اس} \ur{کی} \ur{ساکھ} \ur{جاتی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar dukāndār jhūṭ boltā to us kī sākh jātī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the shopkeeper told lies, his good name would be gone.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ساکھ}} (\emph{sākh}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{sākh}, \textquotedblleft{}evidence, reputation\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{sākṣya}, \textquotedblleft{}testimony\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13322).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sākh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar dukāndār jhūṭ boltā to us kī sākh jātī.} — If the shopkeeper told lies, his good name would be gone.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for one's given word, then the Urdu for honouring a rule, then say \emph{sākh} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نبھنا} (nibhnā)}{نبھنا (nibhnā)}]{\ur{نبھنا} (nibhnā) — to be kept up; to last (of a bond)}

\label{lesson:UR-C531-nibhna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for honouring a rule, then the Urdu for a good name.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نبھنا}}
\textbf{\ur{نبھنا}} — \emph{nibhnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be kept up; to last (of a bond)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{دونوں} \ur{سچے} \ur{ہیں} \ur{تو} \ur{دوستی} \ur{نبھے} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar donoṅ sachche haiṅ to dostī nibhe gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If both of them are true friends, the friendship will last.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{دوستی} \ur{نبھ} \ur{گئی}, \emph{voh dostī nibh gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نبھنا}} (\emph{nibhnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{nibhnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to last, to succeed\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{nirvahati}, \textquotedblleft{}leads out, accomplishes\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 7397).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nibhnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar donoṅ sachche haiṅ to dostī nibhe gī.} — If both of them are true friends, the friendship will last.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for honouring a rule, then the Urdu for a good name, then say \emph{nibhnā} again
\end{itemize}
